messages.content: BRCA1和BRCA2基因在智人和黑猩猩中編碼的蛋白質序列是什麼？

function.name: get_protein_sequence
function.description: Retrieve the protein sequence encoded by a human gene. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species.description: The species for which the gene is to be analyzed.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the protein sequences encoded by BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes in humans and chimpanzees?" They want the protein sequences. We can use the tool get_protein_sequence. We'll need to call it twice per species? Actually we have two genes: BRCA1 and BRCA2. For each gene, we need the protein sequence for Homo sapiens (default) and Pan troglodytes. So four calls: get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA1", species="Homo sapiens"), get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA1", species="Pan troglodytes"), get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA2", species="Homo sapiens"), get_protein_sequence(gene="BRCA2", species="Pan troglodytes"). Then we will output the sequences.

We should check if the function returns the entire protein sequence or maybe just an ID. But likely it returns the amino acid sequence as a string. We'll then format them nicely. Probably we should label them with gene name and species. Also note that the sequences might be long; but we can provide them truncated or full? The user didn't specify length constraints. Provide full sequences. Might be huge (~1863 aa for BRCA1). It's okay.

We'll call the function.
